## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics
- **2026-04-19** — [How I Fully Automated My Video Editing (Claude Code)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G0EH0xdy2-E)  
  Short summary: The workflow uses `Descript` for transcript-based rough cuts, then hands structure and finishing logic to `Claude Code` to standardize edits and exports. Practical setup: upload footage to Descript, run a template that removes repeated takes, verify transcript/cuts manually, then use Claude Code to apply the repeatable edit logic and packaging steps. Available now: yes, using current commercial tools.  
  Why it matters: This is a concrete example of where agentic coding tools are actually useful today: not replacing domain software, but orchestrating repetitive post-production steps around it.

- **2026-04-19** — [From Zero to Your First Agentic AI Workflow in 26 Minutes (Claude Code)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDGiWn0flK8)  
  Short summary: The core tactic is shifting from deterministic drag-and-drop automations to agentic workflows for messy tasks like research, content generation, and support. Practical setup: define the desired outcome, let the agent ask for missing inputs, connect tools/APIs only where needed, and keep human review on outputs that need consistency. Available now: yes, though the evidence here is tutorial-level rather than vendor documentation.  
  Why it matters: The signal is operational, not technical: agentic systems are being positioned as a layer above brittle automation for variable knowledge work.

## 9. Podcast Highlights
- **2026-04-18** — [AI Daily Brief: How to Use Opus 4.7 and the New Codex](https://aidailybrief.beehiiv.com/p/how-to-use-opus-4-7-and-the-new-codex)  
  Short summary: The episode focused on execution patterns for Anthropic Opus 4.7 and OpenAI Codex rather than announcing new products. It framed Codex around persistent operational threads and “chief-of-staff” style task management, and Opus 4.7 around explicit delegation and self-verification prompts.  
  How to use it: For Codex, set up a reusable working thread, keep a running task heartbeat, and use parallel agents only for bounded subtasks. For Opus 4.7, front-load constraints, require explicit checks, and separate planning from execution.  
  References: [Anthropic: Claude Design](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs), [OpenAI: Codex for (almost) everything](https://openai.com/index/codex-for-almost-everything/)  
  Why it matters: The practical shift is from one-shot prompting to managed workflows with memory, delegation, and verification as first-class operating patterns.
